string.text: The ponies of Equestria: earth ponies, pegasi and unicorns under the alicorn princesses.
The gryphons of Griffonstone: proud and tight-fisted, but true to their word.
The hippogriffs of Mount Aris and the seaponies of Seaquestria.
The deer of the northern woods: silent trackers and stubborn archers.
The dragons of the volcanic lands: strength, hoards, and the Gauntlet of Fire for the Bloodstone Scepter.
The yaks of Yakyakistan: loud, honest and very fond of smashing things.
The changelings of the hives: shapeshifters who feed on the love of others.
The heart of Equestria under Princess Celestia, who raises the sun. Canterlot, the old nobility and the Royal Guard — the oldest and proudest of the four Equestrias.
Princess Luna's western lands: cities of night lights, the thestrals of the Night Guard and heroes of old returned from Limbo. Here the night is not a time of fear but of dreams.

The lands of Princess Twilight and the Elements of Harmony: Ponyville, the Castle of Friendship and the busy cities of the east coast. Here they believe friendship is stronger than any army — and keep an army all the same.
The northern empire of the crystal ponies under Princess Cadance, ally of Equestria. While the Crystal Heart stands, Sombra's cold and darkness will not return.
The mountain kingdom of the gryphons, which once lost everything with the Idol of Boreas. The Idol is back now, and the gryphons are learning to be loyal as well as greedy.
The hippogriffs of Mount Aris and the seaponies of Seaquestria. Once they hid from the Storm King beneath the waves; now they fly over their western shore again.
The northern woods and lakes of the deer. A bastard holds the throne, the rightful heir gathers her supporters, and antlered levies watch the border against the dragons.
The scorched south-east of volcanoes and jungle. Dragons respect only strength, but their Dragon Lord Ember is learning that friendship has claws too.
The mountain realm of the yaks. Here they prize plain speech, hard frost and the knack of smashing whatever was done wrong.
The barren south-east, riddled with the hives of the shapeshifters. They feed on the love of others and are preparing a march on their neighbours.
The rabble that follows every war: ruined traders, runaway farmhands and plain idlers with clubs. Alone they are cowards, but a starving mob will face even a patrol.
Guardsponies and militia who dropped their banner mid-campaign. Their weapons are good, their conscience is not, and there is no way back: Equestria judges desertion harshly.
Remnants of the Storm King's army that never laid down their arms after his fall. They come from the sea in black ships and take what their master once promised them.
The dogs dig gems in mountain burrows and find another's labour sweeter than their own. They snatch ponies not from malice but for their nose for precious stones.
Packs of deadwood and vine that assemble themselves in the Everfree thickets. Cut one in half and a day later two of them run the woods.
Scavengers of the wastes beyond the changeling hives. They do not attack the strong: they wait until a caravan weakens from thirst and pick up what is left.
Mounted gangs of the plains who live by raiding herds and wagon trains. They know the steppe better than any patrol and melt into the grass before help arrives.

A company started by Abyssinian cats out of Klugetown now takes whoever comes, and most of all changelings from the nearby hives: they will change shape and work for the feelings of others. The old name is kept on purpose — it commands a higher fee.
Night ponies and thestrals who once served in the Night Guard and now sell their wings. They fight in the dark as surely as others fight by daylight.

Harbour rabble where young dragons have taken the upper hand: scales stop a blow better than any armour, and greed for gold passes for discipline. They are no shame to their town — there, too, no one asks who you are.
The crew of a griffon airship that sails below the clouds and levies toll on the sky roads. Celaeno remembers serving the Storm King and bows to no one now.
Changelings who found home too small after the hives made their peace. They sell what they do best: walk in anywhere behind a borrowed face and strike first.

Hippogriffs find both the land and the sea too narrow, so they hire out where both skills are paid for. Today the band marches along the shore, tomorrow it takes to the water and surfaces behind the enemy.
Griffon rangers settled along the edge of the Everfree who know it better than any pony. For coin they will lead an army through the thickets where the maps run out, and will not ask why.
The unicorn brothers sell cider, tonics and miracles, and when the fraud comes out they wheel their cart to the next county. They hire swords so the takings reach the next fair.
Young dragons left without a cave or a hoard, earning their gold in other people's wars. They fight greedily and briefly: enough for a first pile of treasure, and home they go.
An old earth pony mercenary company with a good name and a high price. They are not the first to run and they do not break a contract — that is what their fame rests on.

Changelings who never accepted the peace between the hives, nor forgave their queen her defeat, yet cannot live without her either. They fight bitterly and for any coin, so long as it is against those who deposed Chrysalis.
Yaks banished from Yakyakistan for rowdiness even by yak standards. No one smashes better, and they hold the line as long as there is something to smash.
Teenage dragons whom the Dragon Lands write off as louts and other people's wars value as expensive shock troops. They have no discipline, but they have claws, wings and a keen wish to show off.

A commune where every cutie mark is the same and talent is declared the root of discord. Those who leave to sell their swords have usually come to doubt equality, but kept the habit of holding formation.
